source.title: Self-Ablating Transformers: More Interpretability, Less Sparsity
source.authors: J. Ferrao; Luhan Mikaelson; Keenan Pepper; Natalia Pérez-Campanero Antolin

record.tranche_reason: It tests neuron explainability using automated explanations scored against activations on new inputs, but in small TinyStories-trained GPT-Neo models rather than the models and audit described in the original claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports mean automated neuron explanation scores for a global-ablation model and a baseline. Its other circuit, SAE, neuron-graph, and language-modeling results do not directly measure the claim versions about neuron-job shares or explanation scores.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Bills et al. simulation-scoring method as a tool to show its self-ablation training improves neuron explainability in 3M-parameter TinyStories models. It reports only mean scores (0.46 vs 0.41), with no share of neurons above a good-score threshold, so it does not bear on whether only a minority of neurons get good scores (V7). It also does not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that self-ablation improves interpretability across ACDC, SAE, explanation-score and N2G tests, at a modest perplexity cost. They also find it decreases overall sparsity (higher L1), which suggests specialization rather than sparsity drives interpretability. The neuron-explanation part is the mean shift from 0.41 to 0.46 for global k=2.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains GPT-Neo models with a self-ablation mechanism and evaluates neuron explanation scores; it does not reproduce the Qwen3-32B pole audit or report the claimed job-category shares.
record.method_sensitivity: The neuron explanation analysis is reported for one self-ablated configuration, global ablation with k=2, and the baseline; no alternative neuron-analysis settings are compared.

fits_no_version.finding: Training with a k-winner-takes-all self-ablation gate raised mean neuron explanation score from 0.41 to 0.46. It also lowered N2G graph density and token diversity in later layers, versus a standard TinyStories-3M model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time selective-activation constraints increase automated neuron explainability and specialization in small language models.

record.problems: The neuron explanation analysis covers one self-ablated configuration and a baseline, uses small TinyStories-trained models, and reports means without uncertainty or a threshold defining a good score. The paper itself notes that its dataset and models are small and that scaling is unknown.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's other reported results concern circuit size, SAE metrics, neuron graphs, perplexity, and L1 norms; these do not directly measure the claim versions about neuron-job shares or new-input explanation scores.

untested.parts: No pole-level job-share audit; no Qwen3-32B.
No comparison of shares across models, MoE or large scales; only 3M-parameter models.
No vision models or canonical polysemantic neuron reanalysis.
No measured share of interpretable neurons under different tools or architectures in the version's sense; no vision models.
No neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models.
No comparison of activating-example fit against prediction of firing.
Fraction of neurons with good simulation scores is not reported; no comparison across explainer strengths.

missing.what: The distribution of per-neuron explanation scores for baseline and self-ablated models is shown as a histogram. It could give the fraction of neurons above a good-score threshold (e.g. 0.8) if read off the figure.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and its limits_scope label are dropped. The rows cannot determine V7, and the study uses Bills scoring only to evaluate its own method. Models are 3M-parameter TinyStories models scored with GPT-4o mini; no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the proportions of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or jobs not understood, and does not study Qwen3-32B.
Does not compare similar shares across models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or large scales.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or recursive generalization versus superposition.
Does not compare interpretability estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models or test the proposed architecture, regularization, and tool explanations.
Does not evaluate attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons or compare them with a trained replacement model.
Does not test whether explanations based on activating examples fail to predict where neurons fire.
Reports mean scores, not the fraction exceeding a stated good-score threshold; tests GPT-4o mini as examiner, not stronger explainer models.

rows.subject: global ablation model with k=2
rows.operation_detail: Generated neuron explanations and scored them by simulating neuron behaviour on new inputs, using correlation between simulated and actual activations.
rows.note: The paper reports a higher mean than the baseline, but gives no threshold or proportion of neurons with good scores.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (self-ablated global k=2 model) compared with its baseline, not a measurement of a version. A mean score of 0.46 gives no share of well-scored neurons.

rows.subject: baseline model
rows.operation_detail: Generated neuron explanations and scored them by simulating neuron behaviour on new inputs, using correlation between simulated and actual activations.
rows.note: Baseline comparison for R1; no threshold or proportion of neurons with good scores is reported.
rows.check: Standard TinyStories-3M baseline, mean simulation score 0.41 (GPT-4o mini explainer). The mean alone cannot show what fraction of neurons score well; no threshold or fraction is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Global ablation k=2 and the baseline model, trained on TinyStories and examined with GPT-4o mini
reader_labels.reason: The study reports mean scores of 0.46 and 0.41 but no good-score cutoff or share of neurons meeting one, so these results do not establish the version's minority-share claim (R1, R2).
